defense_analyst.prose: PHI's pass rush shows up as volume more than results. It blitzes on 23.8% of dropbacks [dc1] and averages 4.2 rushers per dropback [dc2], but its pressure proxy of 11.7% [dc3] over 386 dropbacks [dc4] ranks 31st [dc5], and sacks land on only 5.4% of dropbacks [dc6]. DAL's offense allows a pressure proxy of 16.9% [dc7] over 379 dropbacks [dc8], so expect PHI to send extra rushers and test quick throws and hot routes early. Against the run, PHI allows 0.01 EPA per play [dc9] and an 8.6% explosive rate [dc10] over 269 runs [dc11], with 6.4 defenders in the box on average [dc12]. DAL's run game produces 0.04 EPA per play [dc13] with 6.5 defenders in the box [dc14], so the run game can work against similar boxes. PHI's pass rate over expected ranks 23rd [dc15], so they are not a team that is pushed into obvious passing situations; DAL should not count on forcing them into passing downs. PHI's third-down defense allows conversions on 39.3% of attempts [dc16], ranked 16th [dc17]. Red zone defense allows touchdowns on 57.1% of drives [dc18] over 35 drives [dc19], ranked 14th [dc20]. That red zone sample is small, but it is the area where PHI is most exposed.

Injuries on both sides add rotation questions at linebacker and tight end.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: J.Elliott has made 91.7% [kc1] of field goals on 12 [kc2] attempts and 100.0% [kc3] of 4 [kc4] long-range tries, so treat a long try as a real option, not a lock. sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Philadelphia: WR Dontayvion Wicks is Out (ankle) and has taken 10.5% [ic2] of targets on 306 [ic3] team targets. RB Will Shipley is Questionable (foot) and carries 11.3% [ic5] of rushes on 212 [ic6] rushes. LB Zack Baun is Out (back) and LB Smael Mondon Jr. is Doubtful (ankle), so expect linebacker rotation. sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: The first matchup is PHI's early-down passing against DAL's explosive exposure: PHI throws on 56.4% [mc1] of early downs over 433 [mc2] plays, and Dallas allows explosives on 9.5% [mc3] of pass plays over 401 [mc4] plays. Keep the ball in front of the defense and tackle in space. The second is protection against PHI's extra rushers: PHI blitzes on 23.8% [mc6] of dropbacks, but its pressure proxy is only 11.7% [mc7], ranked 31st [mc8], while Dallas allows 13.5% [mc9] over 458 [mc10] dropbacks, so protection must hold on blitz snaps. The third is the run game: Dallas produces 0.04 [mc11] EPA per run play against a PHI run defense allowing 0.01 [mc12] over 269 [mc13] runs, so run on early downs. In the red zone, PHI allows touchdowns on 57.1% [mc14] of drives over 35 [mc15] drives, so finish with the run and goal-line personnel.
